question: How would you simply describe a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: Any gestation that lasts longer than thirty-six weeks
options.B: A pregnancy that automatically ends in a surgical delivery
options.C: Any pregnancy that occurs in a woman older than twenty years
options.D: A pregnancy where the health of the mother or baby is at increased risk

explanation: You've got this! A high-risk pregnancy just means there are extra health factors that need closer watch to keep both mum and baby safe. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h1)

question: Why is catching a high-risk pregnancy early so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any congenital defects
options.B: It completely stops the mother from experiencing any physical discomfort
options.C: It allows the healthcare team to plan timely interventions and prevent complications
options.D: It removes the need for any laboratory tests during the third trimester

explanation: Spotting risks early gives you and the medical team time to step in and manage things smoothly before they become emergency situations. Great nursing instinct! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h1)

question: Which of these is a classic example of an obstetric risk factor?
explanation: Obstetric factors are linked right to a woman's past pregnancies and birth history, like previous miscarriages or early deliveries. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h2)

question: A pregnant woman who smokes and drinks alcohol falls under which category of risk?
explanation: Behaviors like smoking and alcohol consumption are classified as lifestyle risk factors that can negatively impact fetal development. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h2)

question: What is the hallmark warning sign of placenta previa?

options.B: Sudden swelling of the face and hands
options.D: Severe sharp pain with a rigid abdomen

explanation: Think of placenta previa as the placenta lying low near the cervix. When it bleeds, it's typically painless and bright red—a classic sign to watch out for on the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks comes in with high blood pressure and sudden swelling in her face and hands. What should you suspect?
explanation: New high blood pressure plus sudden swelling after 20 weeks is a major red flag for preeclampsia. Always keep a close eye on your patient's BP readings! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h3)

question: What does a Non-Stress Test (NST) actually check for?

options.A: Fetal heart rate changes in response to movement
options.B: The maturity of the fetal lungs before delivery
options.C: The exact amount of protein in maternal urine
options.D: Maternal blood pressure fluctuations over time

explanation: An NST looks at how the baby's heart rate reacts when they move around. A healthy baby's heart rate speeds up a bit with movement—simple and non-invasive! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h4)

question: Why might doctors order an amniocentesis late in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To treat an active uterine infection
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the growing fetus
options.C: To check if the fetal lungs are mature enough for birth
options.D: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure

explanation: If there's talk of delivering early, a late amniocentesis checks the fluid to see if the baby's lungs are strong and ready to breathe on their own. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h4)

question: Why do doctors often give corticosteroids to a mum facing early labor?

options.A: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing difficulties
options.B: To permanently stop all uterine contractions from happening
options.C: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.D: To lower the mother's blood glucose levels rapidly

explanation: Steroids give a fantastic boost to the baby's developing lungs, helping them avoid serious breathing trouble if they decide to arrive early. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: You are caring for a patient with severe preeclampsia. Which symptom needs your immediate attention?

options.A: An oral temperature of thirty-seven degrees Celsius
options.B: A sudden report of a severe headache and blurred vision
options.C: A slight increase in anxiety about the hospital stay
options.D: A mild increase in appetite during the afternoon shift

explanation: Headaches and blurry vision in preeclampsia mean the brain is under pressure and a seizure might be near. Quick action saves lives here! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h5)

question: Which of these is a critical warning sign that a pregnant woman must report straight away?
explanation: Always teach mums to track their baby's kicks! Fewer movements can mean the baby is stressed and needs an immediate check-up. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: What is the main reason we roll a laboring patient onto her side during an emergency?

options.A: To prepare the patient's back for an epidural anesthetic injection
options.B: To relieve pressure on the vena cava and improve blood flow to the fetus
options.C: To completely stop the progression of active labor contractions
options.D: To make it easier to perform a sterile vaginal examination

explanation: Lying flat lets the heavy uterus press on major blood vessels. Turning her to the side opens up blood flow and sends vital oxygen straight to the baby! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h7)

question: A high-risk mum in labor suddenly has heavy bleeding and a hard, painful belly. What is your FIRST nursing action?

options.A: Administer an oral pain medication to soothe the uterine cramping
options.B: Stop any infusing oxytocin and turn the patient onto her side
options.C: Encourage the patient to push harder to speed up the delivery
options.D: Wait for the primary doctor to arrive before taking any action

explanation: These signs point to a placental abruption. Stopping contractions (oxytocin) and turning her to protect blood flow are your top life-saving priorities! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h7)
